title: Agent Orchestration Incident Tabletop: Provider Failure Cascade
objectives: Restore agent dispatch capability within the configured timeout window by activating tier-based provider escalation.
Preserve plan execution state so that interrupted tasks can be recovered from durable checkpoints rather than re-dispatched from scratch.
Maintain verification gate integrity without bypassing safety controls or suppressing legitimate test failures.
Ensure parallel agents operate in isolated worktrees so that no cross-contamination of branch state occurs during recovery.
Communicate status, decisions, and trade-offs to all role leads at least every five minutes throughout the incident.

roles.name: Incident Commander
roles.responsibility: Owns the response timeline, convenes the bridge, approves all recovery decisions, and ensures stakeholder communication cadence is maintained.

roles.name: Agent Runtime Lead
roles.responsibility: Diagnoses provider and dispatch failures, validates fallback model configuration, and confirms tier-based escalation is active.

roles.name: Operations Engineer
roles.responsibility: Monitors timeout thresholds, assesses partial workspace state from killed tasks, and decides between tuning timeouts and resuming from checkpoint.

roles.name: QA Lead
roles.responsibility: Triages gate failures, determines whether to retry with an escalating model or adjust adaptive thresholds, and documents the trade-off.

roles.name: Platform Infrastructure Lead
roles.responsibility: Manages worktree isolation, enforces workspace_lock_secs, and resolves merge conflicts caused by overlapping agent file access.

roles.name: Reliability Engineer
roles.responsibility: Identifies the last durable BLAKE3 DAG checkpoint, executes plan resume, and confirms state recovery before incident closure.

injects.event: The primary LLM provider begins returning HTTP 503 errors. Agent dispatch tasks stall and several return incomplete output that is persisted as signal.
injects.expected_action: Incident Commander opens the response bridge and assigns roles. Agent Runtime Lead verifies provider status, confirms the failure is not transient, and enables tier-based escalation to the fallback model configured in roko.toml. Incident Commander broadcasts the initial status to all leads.
injects.evidence: RISK-01 mitigation: Configure fallback_model in roko.toml; enable tier-based escalation to next viable provider.

injects.event: A long-running agent task exceeds the 600-second task_attempt_secs threshold and is killed mid-execution, leaving partial workspace state that may corrupt the signal DAG.
injects.expected_action: Operations Engineer assesses the partial state and determines whether it is safe to retain. Incident Commander decides whether to tune [timeouts] in roko.toml for the affected task class or to discard the partial work and recover via --resume-plan from the last checkpoint. The decision and rationale are communicated to all leads.
injects.evidence: RISK-02 mitigation: Tune [timeouts] in roko.toml; use --resume-plan to recover from checkpointed state.

injects.event: cargo test returns a non-zero exit code during the gate run. The 7-rung pipeline short-circuits on first failure and the task cannot pass verification, stalling the plan.
injects.expected_action: QA Lead triages the test failure to distinguish a genuine defect from a flaky test. Incident Commander weighs two options: retry the task with an escalating model, or relax the adaptive threshold after confirming the failure is repeated. The chosen path and its safety trade-off are documented and shared with the bridge.
injects.evidence: RISK-03 mitigation: Retries with escalating models; adaptive thresholds relax on repeated failures.

injects.event: Two parallel agents modify overlapping file paths within a shared worktree, producing merge conflicts and corrupted build artifacts that block downstream tasks.
injects.expected_action: Platform Infrastructure Lead halts parallel execution and invokes the worktree manager to create isolated git worktrees per task. Before resuming, the lead verifies that workspace_lock_secs guards file access and that no two agents target the same paths. Incident Commander confirms isolation is in place before unblocking work.
injects.evidence: RISK-04 mitigation: Worktree manager creates isolated git worktrees per task; workspace_lock_secs guards access.

injects.event: The orchestrator process receives SIGTERM during plan execution before a durable checkpoint is written. In-progress plan execution is at risk of being lost entirely.
injects.expected_action: Reliability Engineer identifies the last persisted content-addressed BLAKE3 DAG record and issues roko plan run plans/ --resume-plan. Incident Commander confirms with each role lead that their recovered state is consistent, then schedules a post-incident review before formally closing the incident.
injects.evidence: RISK-05 mitigation: Use --resume-plan flag; signals persisted as content-addressed BLAKE3 DAG records.

success_criteria: Tier-based escalation to a fallback model is enabled and at least one agent task completes successfully after the provider failure.
Partial workspace state from the timed-out task is either cleanly recovered via --resume-plan or explicitly discarded with documented rationale approved by the Incident Commander.
The verification gate failure is resolved without bypassing the gate pipeline; either a retry with an escalating model or a documented adaptive-threshold adjustment is recorded.
All parallel agents resume in isolated git worktrees with workspace_lock_secs enforced, and no further merge conflicts or artifact corruption occurs.
Plan execution state is recovered from the last durable BLAKE3 DAG checkpoint using --resume-plan, and the incident is formally closed with a post-incident review scheduled.
Status updates with decisions and trade-offs are communicated to all role leads at least every five minutes throughout the incident.
